answer_markdown:
**Short answer:** For a document that is not a will, it must generally be presented for registration within four months from the date of its execution, unless it is a copy of a decree or order, in which case the time limit is four months from the date the decree or order was made, or four months from the date it becomes final [S1]. If the delay in presentation is unavoidable, the Registrar may accept the document for registration if the delay does not exceed four months, upon payment of a fine not exceeding ten times the proper registration-fee [S3].

**What the sources say:**
* No document other than a will shall be accepted for registration unless presented for that purpose to the proper officer within four months from the date of its execution [S1].
* A copy of a decree or order may be presented within four months from the day on which the decree or order was made, or, where it is appealable, within four months from the day on which it becomes final [S1].
* If, owing to urgent necessity or unavoidable accident, any document executed, or copy of a decree or order made, is not presented for registration till after the expiration of the time hereinbefore prescribed in that behalf, the Registrar, in cases where the delay in presentation does not exceed four months, may direct that, on payment of a fine not exceeding ten times the amount of the proper registration-fee, such document shall be accepted for registration [S3].
* For documents purporting to have been executed by all or any of the parties out of India, the registering officer may accept such document for registration if satisfied that the instrument was so executed and that it has been presented for registration within four months after its arrival in India, upon payment of the proper registration-fee [S5].

**How it may apply:**
* If the delay in presentation is unavoidable, an application can be lodged with a Sub-Registrar, who must forward it to the Registrar to whom he is subordinate [S3].
* The rules regarding documents executed out of India require the document to be presented within four months after its arrival in India [S5].

**Uncertain or not covered:** The sources do not specify the time limit for presenting a sale deed in all circumstances, only general rules for documents, decrees/orders, and documents executed out of India [S1][S3][S5]. The specific facts regarding the execution date and the reason for any delay would matter.

**Jurisdiction and date:** Central law as published on India Code; based on texts retrieved on 2026-09-22.
